textAfter: For the first chapter of this story, I’ll begin with where my entire guild history started. HoL.
I had been in another guild before HoL, it’s true.
That guild was called Pirates of Wynn [PoW]
I joined it in early January 2015, when it was a top 10 guild constantly fighting Kangronomicon for the #6 rank. After only a week at most of being in this guild, I went on a hiatus from Wynncraft.

textBefore: Roughly a week in to being a member of HoL, I met with other members at the Troms throne room in what would later be named the “Secret HoL Illuminati Society” or SHIS for short.
At this meeting, myself and 3-4 other members discussed the state of the guild’s leadership and formulated possible plans to remove yosteric from the leadership position.
We ended up deciding on a simple plan: message Spham, the leader of Kangronomicon, and get her to speak to Seb about removing yosteric as the leader.
Kuroi and I were the ones who would execute the plan. We messaged Spham on the forums. Here’s a screenshot.
textAfter: Spham agreed to speak to him, but only if he logged on to Wynn to do it. This presented a dilemma, as he never played Wynn and neither of us knew his Skype.
Kuroi and I discussed the issue for a while, and finally decided that simply speaking to yos might prove to be more beneficial than we thought.
We approached him and made him aware of our grievances with the guild, and he agreed to make us both “Head Chiefs”
This role essentially gave us the power to run the guild in his absence and do what we saw fit.

textBefore: Most of them retreated to Validus, and then later to Libertas when Yos created it.

Obviously this exodus left the guild in a poor state. It took weeks to regain our full strength and become a powerhouse. But as always, the guild prevailed through that troubled time and eventually became one of the top guilds.
That ends the story of my early guild career, along with the HoL coup.
The next part will be the beginnings of the HoL alliance with Fuq & TNA, and the early beginnings of Ordo Malleus.
textAfter: Throughout the entire first part of this story, Validus [Val] had been a constant presence.
It all started months before, on July 5th, 2015.
After warring in the Jungle, yosteric and myself received a message from a Validus Chief named Tangler.
He was interested in the fact that we had been warring against our future ally, Kangronomicon.

textBefore: Around 3-4 guilds were attacking them, all of which were in Concordia. However, the strongest of these guilds was Validus. Validus had become armed with many new members who had left during the HoL Exodus, and among these were a few of our best warring members.
I warred with Kangronomicon for the extent of the attack, coordinating with their chiefs non-stop to ensure that our defense of Wynn was as efficient as possible.
I solod wars for longer than I ever had. When the dust finally settled and we had repelled the attack, it had been 4 hours of non stop warring.
Here is the aftermath of the attack.
textAfter: By the time this had settled, HoL had cemented ourselves for the first time as a powerhouse guild.
After this, we thought the Concordia war was close to being over.
However, it would later be revealed that it was far from over.
The Concordia war would prove to be one of the longest and most brutal that Wynn has ever seen, and would spark the creation of the biggest Mega-alliance of its time, Ordo Malleus.

textAfter: I️ hate to backtrack on the timeline, but here it is a must.
On December 10th, 2016, a couple weeks before where the story left off, a new alliance was created.
It was created from the remnants of Concordia by the traitorous 3zPz
In the alliance contained the ex Concordia guilds as well as many new ones.

textBefore: All the territories were locked down and none could be attacked.
This meant that guilds lucky enough to hold territories got to keep them for the duration of the territory lock.
And considering the Jungle territories were the best territories at the time, no guild benefited more from this glitch than the Toasted Pandas.
Here is a screenshot of when this happened:
textAfter: The territories remained locked for two weeks after Gavel was released, and in this time TnP shot up to level 51.
This was higher than HoL and every other guild except Fuq, TNA, and HHU (who got to that level due to an unintended glitch).
This angered and saddened myself and a few other guilds, who felt that it unfair that TnP should shoot to that level because of a territory lock.
The leaders of TnP also felt that it was unfair and did not desire these seemingly undeserved levels.

textBefore: From then on out it was nothing but a downhill fall.
The alliance would crumble a mere 16 days after TnP left.
That is all for this part. Next time I️ will tell the story of the collapse and what happened afterwards.
textAfter: I️ would like to preface this part with a brief explanation of what I️ have been writing for the past two weeks.

Rather, it is a mixture of both. I️ strive to tell a factually accurate story, with no lies or complete falsities. Along with this factually accurate story, I️ interweave my own perspective and opinions, with careful attention as to not make it nothing but bias.

textAfter: I was not entirely sure who he was or what he meant, but I would later come to find it was him who had organized the alliance that brought down Hax.

A mysterious person within War Syndicate, known only to the rest of the Coalition as “Mr. White” was secretly supplying us with information for months.

textAfter: In the days after our historic victory, we had much to resolve. Going from owning half the map to owning the entire map is no small transition.

Necronomicon had only taken a single territory in the entire invasion, yet we were giving them all of Llevigar. This was 20+ territories, which I think is more than fair.
It is in my belief that they did not read the updates on the map and thought they would be stuck with just their 9 Nemract territories.

textBefore: I immediately came up with an unorthodox solution and proposed it to the remaining leaders: that we merge with the remnants of War Syndicate. There were no other viable allies, and it was the most logical option. I messaged Super, the BCr Co-Leader, but he seemed relatively unresponsive.
A short while after that conversation, Simplyinfinity, the SDU Leader, messaged me and said they would agree to a merger.
We began discussing how it would work, and laid the foundation for the war that was to come, and the alliance that was to come.
textAfter: At first, our makeshift alliance had no name. We were simply a few leaders sitting and talking. The name “Federation” began as a joke, considering Coalition had also been named just by being a synonym for alliance, I joked we should do it again with the name Federation, but people liked it and it became our name.

We began to organize and copied the exact same structure that Coalition had, and then set our sights on the map. There were small skirmishes, but at the beginning nobody had the morale to attack, and nothing truly organized happened.

The fighting began with a lone chief from HoF. Her name was Snowythewolf. She had remembered the leaders of ERN speaking about their low bank in Coalition, and made the decision to begin attacking their Llevigar territories. She fought for countless hours, and was able to hold her own for quite some time, warring so much that the leaders of THI had to join HoF to war for the night so that she could sleep.

I began warring for Llevigar as well on the night of February 17th, and continued until about 3 AM the 18th. When I went to sleep, Llevigar was firmly under the control of Emorians. Curiously however, I noted that despite going bankrupt, they were still defended with the full 1000 mobs, and seeing as this was before the mob update, this cost roughly 2.5k emeralds per defense.

textBefore: Fuq also slowed down their war efforts, and they mostly stopped warring.
At this point, AA was no longer a real threat to the Federation and I would say it was around this time that the war officially ended, with a decisive Federation victory.

The map was secure, the alliance was stronger than ever, and we had no true organized enemies left. However, this peace and quiet was the perfect breeding ground for old rivalries and resentments to remerge, and the alliance would soon go through it’s most unstable and volatile period in history.
textAfter: (Help I’ve run out of images someone please give me ideas I’ll accept practically anything over this egotistical excuse for a chapter header)
Aside from its final days, early Federation was the most unstable point in the alliance’s existence.
The first 2 months of an alliance’s lifespan are always the most crucial, it is in that time that empires are either forged or smothered. And Federation was no different.
The first indication of trouble came before AA retook the map. BCr, who did not participate in the first battle whatsoever, decided that they were unhappy with the territories they were designated.

textBefore: The vote was standard except for an addendum that nobody would be forced to war against BCr since many guilds in Federation were still friends with Tnt and didn’t want to kick him if it meant they’d have to fight.

Another unnecessary fact I feel needs clarifying due to the sheer amount of historical revisionism it’s gone through: Tnt will claim that he left Federation, and while this is technically true, he simply pulled a Nixon. The vote was 100% going to end with him kicked, he simply left everything before the vote finished so that he could tell everyone he wasn’t kicked.

With Tnt finally gone, Federation entered one of its most prosperous periods. The next few months were fairly stable and easily some of the least drama filled in the alliance’s history, despite growing opposition from Tnt’s new alliance and its countless splinters. However, in my opinion the sheer havoc he was able to wreak from the inside was far more of a threat than anything he was ever able to do from the outside. It is a minor miracle that the alliance survived its first few months, and many more such miracles would have to occur before the alliance would finally succumb.
textAfter: The next few months ran smoothly. For the most part, the alliance had no major issues. There were arguments, of course. Guilds left. Guilds were kicked. But for the most part, it was peaceful. Federation had established itself as the dominant force, and the enemy alliances Tnt kept forming were too weak and splintered apart at every chance.

I could make some attempt to drone on and on about this time period, but it has been almost 3 years at this point, and my memory of everything other than significant events has almost entirely vanished. Instead, I will cover the highlights. The most interesting and memorable events.

Early in April, Thunder had become far too addicted to watching anime to effectively continue his ownership of HoL, and he informed me that he would like to leave Federation and go inactive. He first informed me of this on April 1st, and since I trust no man on April Fool’s Day, I told him I would ignore him until he told me the same tomorrow.

Truth be told, I knew he was serious. I just loved having him as a close ally, and he was the only person I have ever trusted with ownership of HoL. I was hoping he might sleep on it and reconsider, but he didn’t. Once again HoL was returned to the dirt, cold and dead.

At the end of July 2018, I awoke to some drama. My girlfriend had been involved on some kind of argument in the Federation discord, and although I am still fuzzy on the details, it became clear that everyone blamed her for the fallout afterward. A vote was started to kick her guild. She left the alliance before it could complete. I broke up with her immediately after this. There were issues in the relationship, just as any, you can imagine. But for the most part looking back, I believe I made this decision primarily because I saw my own girlfriend as an inconvenience to my plans for Wynncraft.
